components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single main action in a decision area.

components.description: A lower-priority action with familiar neutral treatment.

narrative.overview: Carecierge should feel like the quiet desk in a well-run boutique hotel: warm, discreet, capable, human, and organized. The product is friendly and familiar, but it never turns relationship care into performance, surveillance, or sentimentality.

rules.name: The Ten Percent Accent Rule
rules.body: Concierge Moss is rare by default. If more than 10% of a working screen is accented, the product starts to feel decorative instead of trustworthy.

rules.name: The Semantic Red Rule
rules.body: Red stays under 5% of a working screen and appears only for destructive actions, irreversible decisions, or critical errors.

rules.name: The Clean Surface Rule
rules.body: Warmth comes from guidance, rhythm, and accent choices, not from beige body backgrounds.

rules.name: The Discreet Depth Rule
rules.body: If the shadow is the first thing a user notices, it is too heavy.

dos: Do reuse the semantic palette before considering any new color.
Do keep primary actions clear, rare, and visually trustworthy.
Do make automation explainable, reversible, and visibly in service of the user's intent.
donts: Don't use red as a decorative accent.
Don't use generic chatbot scaffolding as the product's main visual metaphor.
Don't use hearts, pink gradients, cheesy intimacy language, or couple-tracking aesthetics.
